figure: Figure 8.1 — Where inference computation and data movement actually live
issue: The red gradient arrow ('capacity grows / speed drops / distance grows') spans vertically from the registers row down through the tensor-cores/ALU row to the HBM row, visually implying a single size/speed ladder that includes the compute group. The caption explicitly states 'compute, memory and interconnect are separate groups in this figure, not levels of one ladder,' but the figure's own visual encoding contradicts this by drawing one continuous arrow across group boundaries.
evidence: Rendered page: the red double-headed arrow's top endpoint is adjacent to the 'small · fast · close' label at the registers row; its bottom endpoint is adjacent to 'large · slow' at the HBM row. The tensor-cores row (blue, compute group) lies between them. A reader glancing at the figure without the caption would reasonably read all five rows as one ladder.
acceptance_test: Either (a) break the gradient arrow into two segments that span only the memory rows (registers → HBM) skipping over the tensor-cores row, or (b) add a visual gap/bracket showing the arrow applies only to orange rows, or (c) reposition the arrow so it clearly runs alongside only the memory-hierarchy rows.

issue: The caption states 'the faint vertical rules inside the KV band mark those 24.9 GB request slots,' but at print size the rules are extremely faint — barely distinguishable from the dotted background pattern of the orange KV band.
evidence: Rendered page at 150 dpi: the vertical rules are present but their contrast against the orange dotted fill is very low; at actual print size on uncoated paper they would likely be invisible or confused with the dot pattern.
acceptance_test: Increase the stroke contrast of the vertical rules (e.g., darker line color or solid vs dotted distinction) so they are clearly visible at print size, or remove the caption reference if the rules cannot be made legible.
